title: Report: sideloaded fake "Google Chrome" extension steals Microsoft and Google session cookies and captures webcam frames
date_note: The GBHackers page gives only its own publication day; the date of the researchers' finding was not stated on the page read.
geo_basis: No victim location is stated; pin placed on the researcher (Palo Alto Networks, Santa Clara, USA)
summary: GBHackers, relaying Palo Alto Networks research, reports a malicious browser extension disguised as "Google Chrome" that victims had to sideload after enabling Developer Mode. According to the article it captures keystrokes and authentication cookies for Microsoft and Google accounts, and captures webcam frames. The researchers assess with moderate confidence that Helix-associated attackers built it.
plain: GBHackers, relaying Palo Alto Networks research, describes a fake "Google Chrome" extension that victims had to install by hand. It steals keystrokes and sign-in cookies for Microsoft and Google accounts and captures webcam frames.
exec: Palo Alto Networks research, as relayed by GBHackers, shows a sideloaded extension that takes session cookies for Microsoft and Google accounts.
action: The researchers, as relayed by GBHackers, advise browser-extension allowlists, stronger helpdesk identity verification, phishing-resistant MFA, and hunting for the extension ID and connections to oskeysetup[.]com.

validation.note: Only GBHackers was read; the original research report could not be found by search, so the findings are relayed second-hand.
